questions.heading: Check k Against What the Plan Must and Can Fund Before You Solve
questions.stem: A rule asks for at least 3 projects from a group of three: P1, P2 and P3, where P1 and P2 are the repair and replace options for one asset (an alternative group). The solver reports INFEASIBLE. What does a precheck of the group find?

options.text: 3 candidates for a minimum of 3, so the group passes and another row is to blame
options.says: Candidates in one alternative group count once; counting all three is the mistake the precheck avoids.

options.text: At most 2 of them fit in one plan, since P1 and P2 count once, so none reaches 3
options.says: Right: one of P1 and P2 plus P3 is the most any plan can fund, as with Plains' two transmission options.

options.text: At most 1 of them fits in one plan, since an alternative group blocks the others
options.says: The alternative row limits P1 and P2 to one between them; it says nothing about P3.

options.text: No plan fits, since every at-least row over an alternative group is infeasible
options.says: An at-least row is infeasible only when the minimum exceeds what can be chosen; at least 2 here would be fine.

questions.heading: At Most One of Many Is One Row, Not One Row per Pair
questions.stem: Five projects all share one outage, so every two of them conflict. Analyst A writes 10 rows x_a + x_b <= 1, one per pair. Analyst B writes one row: the sum of all five is at most 1. Which is true?

options.text: B's rows allow 0/1 plans that A's refuse, so B's optimum can be higher
options.says: Two funded projects break both one pair row and the sum row, so the 0/1 plans are the same.

options.text: A's rows allow 0/1 plans that B's refuse, so A's optimum can be higher
options.says: Any 0/1 plan with two funded projects breaks a pair row, so A refuses it too.

options.text: Both allow the same 0/1 plans, and B's LP relaxation can give the looser bound
options.says: The pair rows allow 0.5 on every project, a sum of 2.5; the single row allows a sum of 1, so B's bound is the tighter.

options.text: Both allow the same 0/1 plans, and A's LP relaxation can give the looser bound
options.says: Right: the relaxation of the pair rows admits fractional points the sum row refuses, as with the Valley line.

questions.heading: None, or at Least k, Needs a Switch Variable
questions.stem: A paving contractor takes a district only if it gets at least 3 jobs there. The district has 5 candidate jobs; n is the number funded and g a binary. Which pair of rows states "none, or at least 3"?

options.says: Right: g = 0 forces n to 0, and g = 1 asks for at least 3 of the 5.
With g = 0 nothing bounds n above by 0, so 1 or 2 jobs are allowed.
n >= 3 holds for every plan, so "none" is never allowed.
With g = 0 this asks for n >= 3 and n <= 0 at once, and with g = 1 it allows any count from 0 to 5, including 1 and 2.
